channel.title: Use & Like: app news
channel.description: What changed in the apps you use, in our own words, with what it means for you and what to do about it.

item.title: Alexa Plus explained: cost, free with Prime, devices and countries
item.description: Alexa+ is Amazon's AI version of Alexa: it's included with Prime and costs $19.99 a month without it in the US, it's open to everyone in the US and Canada, and this year it has reached 11 more countries through early access, Japan last on 29 October.

item.title: Hello Moon: ambient music app for iPhone that follows the Moon's phase
item.description: Hello Moon plays ambient music that changes with the Moon's current phase, with its own composed themes for each of the eight phases. The $3.99 app came out on 7 November and was #31 in Music on the US App Store's paid chart on 22 November.

item.title: How to turn off AI features in Canva, Gemini and Signal explained
item.description: In one week Canva added a switch that turns off its generative AI tools, Google split Gemini's settings so you can keep chat history but stop AI training, and Signal began blocking screenshots so phone assistants can't read your chats, but each switch covers less than its name suggests.

item.title: iTell app: use your Android phone's second number on your iPhone
item.description: iTell connects an Android phone to your iPhone over Bluetooth, so you can take and make its calls, read and answer its texts and see its contacts from the iPhone. The free iPhone app came out on 8 November and was #55 in Utilities on the US App Store's free chart on 22 November.

item.title: Siri AI daily limit explained: what counts and how to get more
item.description: With iOS 27.3, Siri AI keeps simple requests unlimited but pauses multi-step and writing requests once a device hits its daily limit, and only an iCloud+ plan of 200 GB or more raises that limit, much like Gemini and ChatGPT tie heavier use to paid plans.

item.title: Windows 11 lets antivirus run outside the kernel to cut blue screens
item.description: Microsoft's new Windows endpoint security platform, now generally available on Windows 11, lets security apps do their checks outside the Windows kernel, so a faulty update is less likely to crash the PC. Bitdefender Antivirus Free and Sophos plan support by the end of 2026.

item.title: Apple Siri settlement claim: about $61 per iPhone, deadline December 21
item.description: US buyers of an iPhone 15 Pro, 15 Pro Max or any iPhone 16 model can claim money from Apple's $250 million Siri settlement until December 21. Lawyers for the buyers estimated on November 16 that each eligible iPhone will likely get at least $61, with $95 as the most per phone.

item.title: Billable Timer app: track billable hours on iPhone and iPad
item.description: Billable Timer: Time Tracker is a $4.99 app for people who bill by the hour, such as lawyers, accountants and consultants, with no in-app purchases. It was #33 among paid Business apps on the US App Store on 22 November.

item.title: Clicks Communicator delay: keyboard phone now ships in 2027
item.description: Clicks has moved deliveries of its $649 Communicator keyboard phone from December to late January and February 2027. People who ordered before 20 November get a pair of 3.5mm wired headphones in the box.

item.title: Copilot will rename and move files for you on Windows 11
item.description: Microsoft showed at Ignite 2026 that Copilot will soon move, rename and sort files in folders like Downloads and Desktop when you ask in plain words. Microsoft calls it local file actions and hasn't given a date.

item.title: Dayclipse app: sunrise, golden hour and moon phase tracker
item.description: Dayclipse: Sun & Moon Tracker is a $4.99 app that shows sunrise, sunset, golden hour, blue hour and moon phases for any place, and works offline. It was #29 among paid Weather apps on the US App Store on 21 November.

item.title: Digital ID at TSA explained: Apple Wallet, Google Wallet, state apps
item.description: You can show a digital ID on your phone at TSA checkpoints in more than 250 US airports, by tapping the reader or scanning a QR code, but TSA still wants every traveler to carry a physical ID as well.

item.title: Doxology Way prayer app: daily prayers for five Christian traditions
item.description: Doxology Way is a $9.99 daily prayer app that follows the prayers, readings and saints of the tradition you pick: Orthodox, Catholic, Anglican, Lutheran or Protestant and Evangelical. It was #55 among paid Reference apps on the US App Store on 21 November.

item.title: Fitbit third-party apps and clock faces end on November 28
item.description: From 28 November you can't install or update third-party apps and clock faces on Fitbit Sense and Versa watches; only Fitbit's and Google's own stay in the gallery. What's already on your watch keeps working, but a deleted app or a factory reset means it's gone for good.

item.title: Gemini camera on Android redesigned: it now opens inside your chat
item.description: The camera you open from the plus menu in Gemini's prompt box now slides up as a sheet over your chat on Android, instead of a separate full-screen viewfinder. It has rolled out widely with Google app version 17.76 and later, after reaching the iPhone app first.

item.title: iPhone Duo fold test explained: how many folds the hinge can take
item.description: CNET's folding machine passed 451,000 folds on the iPhone Duo by 13 November with the phone still working but the hinge loosening, while Apple hasn't published a fold rating of its own.

item.title: iPhone Duo spatial photos and videos: Duo Spatial camera app
item.description: Duo Spatial is a $1.99 camera app made only for the foldable iPhone Duo that takes spatial photos and videos for Apple Vision Pro, picking the camera pair by how far the phone is unfolded. It was #97 among paid Photo & Video apps on the US App Store on 21 November.

item.title: Lumiri Todo: a pay-once to-do and daily planner app for iPhone and Mac
item.description: Lumiri Todo: Daily Planner is a $2.99 to-do app with no subscription and no in-app purchases, for iPhone, iPad and Mac. It was #89 among paid Productivity apps on the US App Store on 21 November.

item.title: makeART Coloring Book app for iPhone and iPad, with no ads
item.description: makeART Coloring Book is a $7.99 colouring app for iPhone and iPad where you tap to fill pages or paint with brushes. It came out on 20 November and was #30 among paid Graphics & Design apps on the US App Store on 21 November.

item.title: MeroMusic: music notation app for iPhone with VoiceOver support
item.description: MeroMusic is a $10 app for iPhone and iPad that puts a score editor, playable instruments and a recording studio in one place. It came out on 18 November and was #60 among paid Music apps on the US App Store on 21 November.

item.title: My Anti-Rot Year: journal app to cut endless scrolling
item.description: My Anti-Rot Year is a $6.99 year-long journal app for iPhone and iPad for people who lose their evenings to scrolling. It came out on 20 November and was #40 among paid Productivity apps on the US App Store on 21 November.

item.title: Orbit app launcher for iPhone puts your apps on a 3D wheel
item.description: Orbit: Quick Launch Wheel is a $2.99 app launcher for iPhone that lines up the apps you open most on a spinning 3D wheel you flick and tap. It came out on 20 November and was #49 among paid Productivity apps on the US App Store on 21 November.

item.title: Orivo day planner app for iPhone turns timetable photos into events
item.description: Orivo: Day Planner & Calendar is a $3.99 iPhone planner that shows what's happening now at the top and can turn a photo or screenshot of a class timetable or work roster into calendar events. It was #98 among paid Productivity apps on the US App Store on 21 November.

item.title: Parental controls on iPhone vs Android: setting up a kid's phone
item.description: On an iPhone, parental controls come from a Child Account in Family Sharing and Screen Time; on Android, from Google's Family Link, and Family Link can't supervise an iPhone, so the child's phone decides which system you use.

item.title: Planescope flight radar app for iPhone shows the planes above you
item.description: Planescope: Live Air Traffic is a $1.99 flight radar app that shows the aircraft flying around you on an animated radar, turned to the direction you face. It was #62 among paid Travel apps on the US App Store on 21 November.

item.title: Salon app turns Apple TV into an art frame with museum paintings
item.description: Salon is an Apple TV app that keeps one picture on your TV screen like a frame on the wall: over 1,000 open-access museum paintings, or your own photos from iCloud. It costs 9.99 dollars once, with no subscription mentioned.

item.title: Today planner app: tasks, recipes and links in one box
item.description: Freedom Forge Today is a $1.99 planner for iPhone, iPad, Mac and Apple Watch that sorts what you type, paste or share into Today, Soon and Someday instead of due dates. It came out on 21 November and was #31 among paid Productivity apps on the US App Store the same day.

item.title: Untitled Starry Sky AI art app turns sketches and photos into art
item.description: Untitled Starry Sky is a free iPhone and iPad app that turns a written idea, a photo or a few drawn strokes into a collage, geometric or abstract painting with AI. It was #60 among free Graphics & Design apps on the US App Store on 21 November.

item.title: Very Good Camera app for iPhone: three film looks for $9.99
item.description: Very Good Camera is a $9.99 iPhone camera app with three film-style colour grades from Very Good Co.: VG400 for any light, VG800 for low light and VGTX for black and white. It was #26 among paid Photo & Video apps on the US App Store on 21 November.

item.title: Waypoints travel log app for iPhone saves places you want to visit
item.description: Waypoints is a $2.99 travel log app for iPhone, iPad and Mac where you save restaurants, cafes, hotels and sights, grouped by city and trip. It was #59 among paid Travel apps on the US App Store on 21 November.

item.title: Weathercloud app for iPhone shows live weather from real stations
item.description: Weathercloud Network is a free iPhone app that shows live readings from more than 150,000 weather stations around the world, run by professionals and hobbyists. It was #70 among free Weather apps on the US App Store on 21 November.

item.title: Windows 11 new search bar arrives in optional update KB5132057
item.description: Windows 11's new taskbar search, rebuilt without web parts, is coming to PCs with the optional November update KB5132057. It opens faster, shows one short list of results and can switch brightness, Bluetooth or dark mode from there.

item.title: ZIV Live: wedding photo sharing with a QR code, no app needed
item.description: ZIV Live collects the photos and videos guests take at a wedding or party into one private gallery: they scan a QR code and upload, with no app or account. You pay once per event, from $5.

item.title: Signal blocks screenshots to keep Siri AI and Gemini out of chats
item.description: Signal now stops screenshots inside its app on iPhone and Android, so AI assistants built into the phone can't read your messages off the screen. On Android it switches on Screen security by itself when it detects an assistant trying to read the screen; on iOS 27 a new Block Siri AI setting does the job.

item.title: Android App Lock won't come to older Android versions, Google says
item.description: Android's built-in App Lock needs a full Android update and can't be added to older versions through Google Play system updates, Google's Mishaal Rahman said on 20 November. Google plans to ship it with Android 17 QPR3 in the first quarter of 2027.

item.title: App Launcher widget for iPhone puts 100+ apps on one home screen page
item.description: App Launcher: Home Screen is a free iPhone and iPad app that turns one full-page widget into a grid of more than 100 app icons, plus two lock screen widgets with eight apps each. It was #89 among free Graphics & Design apps on the US App Store on 20 November.

item.title: Apple Music streams GTA 6 CircoLoco radio DJ sets live on 22 November
item.description: Apple Music Club radio is livestreaming DJ sets from The Vault Presents CircoLoco Records Radio, tied to Grand Theft Auto VI's in-game station, on Sunday 22 November at 8 PM. Digital Music News says fans can listen for free.

item.title: Apple Pay not working: new reports on 20 November after the outage
item.description: Downdetector showed a new rise in Apple Pay complaints on Friday, 20 November, three days after Apple's outage on Tuesday. Apple hadn't confirmed a new problem.

item.title: AT&T landline in California: FCC backs plan to end copper phone lines
item.description: The FCC has overruled California rules that made AT&T get the state's approval before ending old copper landline service. AT&T has proposed ending that service in California on or after 1 June 2027, according to the state's utilities commission.

item.title: Baby tracker app with no subscription: Baby Log & Head Time
item.description: Baby Log & Head Time is a $4.99 one-time iPhone app for logging feedings, naps, diapers, baths and doctor visits with one tap each. It was #42 among paid Health & Fitness apps on the US App Store on 20 November.

item.title: Booking.com scam on WhatsApp uses real booking details to demand payment
item.description: Scammers are messaging travellers on WhatsApp with their real names, emails and hotel details, claiming to be Booking.com or Expedia and demanding a quick payment through a link or the booking gets cancelled. New Zealand's Travel Agents Association says it's happening daily.

item.title: Brave iPhone update 1.99 adds iPhone Duo support and Top Sites choice
item.description: Brave version 1.99 for iPhone, on the App Store since 18 November, now fits Apple's foldable iPhone Duo and lets you choose what the new tab page shows.

item.title: ChatGPT CarPlay: dot users can now call their dot from the car
item.description: You can now call your ChatGPT dot from Apple CarPlay and ask about a task it's already working on, as OpenAI's Romain Huet showed in a video on 20 November. A regular ChatGPT Voice chat in CarPlay starts fresh each time.

item.title: ChatGPT Space rolls out to Plus users with pages and presentations
item.description: OpenAI started rolling out ChatGPT Space to Plus subscribers aged 18 and over worldwide on November 20; until now it was for Pro, Business and Enterprise plans. In Space you build interactive pages and presentations with ChatGPT, and they can update themselves from connected apps and tools.

item.title: Claude and the Riemann hypothesis: Anthropic mathematician claims a proof
item.description: Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at Anthropic, says he found a proof of the Riemann hypothesis while working with Claude and posted it on November 20 as a four-page statement plus a proof written in Lean, a language that checks every step. Mathematicians haven't accepted it yet, and the Clay Mathematics Institute still lists the problem as unsolved.

item.title: Fake Tax Authority app hijacks Android phones, Israel warns
item.description: Israel's National Cyber Directorate warned on 19 November about messages that lead to a fake Google Play page offering a Tax Authority app. Once installed and given permissions, it lets attackers read text messages and one-time codes, turn on the camera and control the phone.

item.title: Frame Pro Camera app: RAW iPhone photos with film-style looks
item.description: Frame: Pro Camera is a $9.99 iPhone camera app that shoots RAW and develops the photos with film-style colour and grain instead of the iPhone's usual processing. It was #77 among paid Photo & Video apps on the US App Store on 20 November.

item.title: GasSavvy gas price app counts your discounts before ranking stations
item.description: GasSavvy is a new 1.99 dollar iPhone app that ranks nearby gas stations by what a full tank would cost you after the discounts you already have, such as Walmart+, Shell Fuel Rewards, Exxon Mobil Rewards+, T-Mobile Tuesdays, AAA or AARP. It came out on 19 November and was #12 among paid Travel apps on the US App Store on 20 November.

item.title: Gemini GIF maker: Gemini now creates animated GIFs from a prompt
item.description: The Gemini app can now make short looping GIFs from a text prompt, a photo or a video. Google announced it on 20 November: it's rolling out to Google AI subscribers worldwide and to free users in eight countries, including the US and the UK.

item.title: Google Fi app redesign on Android adds Ask Fi AI support button
item.description: Google Fi's Android app has moved its tabs into a floating bar and added an Ask Fi button that opens Google's AI support chat. It's rolling out with app version 171.
